finding: §4's emission condition and §2's blocking set exclude each other, so two of §4's paragraphs and one test row specify a population that can never be observed. §4 emits by_severity 'when the merged round would be clean under the resolved policy AND holds at least one non-PASS row'. §2 defines clean under blocking as 'no non-PASS row in the round carries a blocking severity', and the blocking severities are error plus every unrecognised shape. Therefore in EVERY round where by_severity is emitted, the error bucket and the unrecognised bucket are necessarily 0. §4's stated invariant -- 'error + unrecognised sums the round's blocking rows and the two sections cannot drift apart' -- is always 0 = 0 on the only surface it is stated for. §7 test 17 is not merely weak, it is unwritable: its fixture 'carrying all four unrecognised shapes' is by construction a round that does not emit the key, and both wrong implementations it names (an empty-string bucket, splitting the four) also pass, because the buckets they corrupt are empty. §4 closes the second branch itself: 'Under all the condition is unreachable by construction'. Wrong if: §4 emitted by_severity on every merged round holding a non-PASS row, or §2's blocking set excluded unrecognised -- either makes the buckets reachable.
suggestion: Decide which surface carries the buckets and say so; do not keep both. (a) Replace §4's emission condition with 'Emitted on every merged round that holds at least one non-PASS row, and it survives --compact', delete the paragraph justifying the clean half, and test 17 becomes writable as written. Or (b) keep the clean-gated emission, delete the error/unrecognised buckets and test 17, and replace the invariant sentence with: 'On an emitted round every bucket is advisory by construction -- an error row or an unrecognised one would have made the round unclean, so the key never has to distinguish them.'

finding: §7 test 13 and §3 give opposite answers about the same write. Test 13: the writes that must pass are 'any write of all, and an import carrying an already-resolved blocking forward'. §3, four paragraphs earlier: 'a --project write of all that *uncovers* a task override of blocking changes the resolved value and must be refused.' An engineer writing test 13 from the row ships a fence that lets the uncovering write through; one writing it from §3 ships a test the row calls a failure. Neither of §3's two worked cases -- the --project write of blocking under a task override of all that must PASS, and the --project write of all that uncovers blocking and must be REFUSED -- appears in test 12 or 13. So §3's longest normative passage, the one defining the comparison as resolved-before against resolved-after at every sink, has no row deriving from it. Wrong if: §3's 'Resolved means resolved' paragraph did not exist, or test 13 read 'any write of all that does not uncover a higher-layer blocking'.
suggestion: Rewrite test 13's assertion as: 'the writes that must **pass**: a write of all that leaves the resolved value all; a --project write of blocking under a task override of all, which changes nothing an audit reads; and an import carrying an already-resolved blocking forward -- three assertions'. Then add row 13b: '| 13b | §3 *resolved not stored* | a --project write of all that uncovers a task override of blocking is refused, because the resolved value changes to blocking | a fence comparing the written literal instead of resolved-before against resolved-after |'.

finding: §3 states the fence unconditionally and §7 test 12 silently narrows it, so the release as specified ships a knob nobody can set and §7 holds no row that would notice. §3's normative sentence is 'The fence refuses a write that CHANGES the resolved value to blocking', with no attended/unattended distinction anywhere in the section -- a regex search for 'unattended|UNATTENDED|tp run' over spec/0.37.0.md returns exactly four lines (140, 141, 149 and test row 278) and none is a scoping clause. Test 12 introduces TP_UNATTENDED=1 for the first time, as a test condition rather than as a rule. Read literally, §3 refuses every write of blocking including the operator's, which makes §1's deliverable 1 unreachable; read via test 12, the fence is inert without the variable, and no row asserts that an attended write of blocking succeeds and resolves. §3's own table argues for the narrow reading without stating it: row 1's tp import deadlock is qualified 'under tp run', which is only a deadlock if attended imports pass. Wrong if: §3 named TP_UNATTENDED as the condition, and §7 carried the attended-path row.
suggestion: Add to §3 immediately after the change-rule sentence: 'The refusal is the unattended fence: it fires when TP_UNATTENDED is set, on the same terms as the four decisions already reserved for the operator. Attended, the same write succeeds -- that is what makes the field opt-in rather than absent.' Then add row 12b: '| 12b | §3 *the fence* | with TP_UNATTENDED unset, a write of blocking on each of the three paths exits 0 and the field resolves to blocking -- three assertions | a fence that refuses unconditionally, which ships an unsettable knob and passes test 12 |'.

finding: §4 asserts '--merge can evaluate that condition -- it holds the round's rows and resolves the same field --record will.' It cannot resolve the same field, and the code says why. internal/cli/audit_merge.go lines 26-37 reject a spec-looking positional at entry with exit 2 ('--merge takes NDJSON input files only'), so tp audit --merge is structurally never told which spec the round belongs to. §2 puts *task override* at the top of the precedence, and that layer lives in <base>.tasks.json keyed by the spec base. Whenever a task override is set, --merge and --record can resolve different values and §4's emission condition then fires on one command and not the other. §7 tests 15, 16 and 17 all assert by_severity without pinning which layer --merge read, so an implementation consulting only the project config passes all three, and so does one consulting the active pointer instead. Wrong if: §4 named the layers --merge reads, or this release gave --merge a way to learn the spec.
suggestion: State the resolution --merge actually performs, in §4: 'Because --merge takes only NDJSON inputs and refuses a spec-looking positional, it resolves audit_converge_on from the project config and the built-in only -- a task override does not reach it. Where the two layers disagree, --merge's breakdown is advisory and --record's verdict governs.' Add row 15c: '| 15c | §4 *resolution* | with a task override of blocking over a project config of all, --merge follows the project layer and --record follows the override, and the spec names which is authoritative | a fixture with no task override, where the two layers cannot disagree |'.

finding: §7 test 15's absent case is 'an all-PASS round', which does not discriminate the implementation §4 explicitly rejects. §4 says an earlier draft 'took the count half and dropped the clean half, which puts the key on every round that has any finding'. A count-only implementation emits nothing on an all-PASS round too, because the count is zero -- so test 15 passes under the very draft §4 spends a paragraph rejecting, and its named failing input ('emitting unconditionally') is a strictly weaker mutant that the count-only draft is not. The two cases that separate the drafts are absent from §7 entirely: a round NOT clean under blocking that holds non-PASS rows, and any round under audit_converge_on: all that holds non-PASS rows. Wrong if: test 15's absent case named an unclean round holding findings rather than an all-PASS round.
suggestion: Split test 15 into two rows: '| 15 | §4 | by_severity is present on a round clean under blocking that holds non-PASS rows | emitting unconditionally |' and '| 15b | §4 *the clean half* | **absent** on a round holding error rows under blocking, and absent on a round holding non-PASS rows under all -- the two cases an all-PASS round cannot separate | the count-only draft §4 rejects, which passes an all-PASS absent case |'.

finding: §7 test 9 asserts that switching to blocking 'leaves every stored round's **reported** verdict unchanged -- reported, not stored'. There is no emitted form of 'every stored round's verdict'. tp audit --status/--record report clean for the LATEST round only (internal/cli/audit_signal_test.go reads out[round], out[clean], out[consecutive_clean] off one payload); the only surface carrying every round's verdict is state.json, which the row forbids by name. So the row is writable only as a one-round assertion, and the multi-round property §2 actually decides -- that engine.ConsecutiveClean over the stored rounds does not move when the knob flips -- is asserted by nothing in §7. The row's justification is separately unverifiable from the spec: §2 says 'the review twin recomputes live', the row says 'the twin stamps too'. Both are true of the code (internal/engine/reviewstate.go:20 stores 'Clean bool'; internal/cli/review_record.go:194 reports a recomputed liveClean), but §2 states only half, so a reader of §2 alone concludes the row's premise is false and writes the stored-bytes assertion the row forbids. Wrong if: the row named an emitted per-round list, or asserted consecutive_clean and converged rather than a per-round verdict.
suggestion: Make the observable the aggregate, which is emitted. Rewrite test 9: 'recording n rounds under all and then setting blocking without re-recording leaves clean, consecutive_clean and converged on --status byte-identical to their values before the switch | a live re-grade at read time'. And complete §2's stamping paragraph: 'The review twin does both -- it stores a clean flag on the round and reports a recomputed one. Only the reported value separates the two designs, which is why the audit side is specified on what it reports.'

finding: §7 test 18 asserts 'all **nine** surviving assertions of the gate guard still pass' and §6a item 1 says 'Two of its eleven assertions; the other nine stand'. The spec names neither the file, the test function, nor the counting rule, so the number is unreproducible from the spec. Counted here: TestAuditGate_NoEscapeHatchFromTheGate in internal/cli/audit_signal_test.go lines 469-503 holds 11 assert./require. call sites -- lines 473, 474, 481, 484, 485, 490, 493, 494, 497, 498, 500, from a regex faster_search for '(assert|require)' followed by a dot over that file, restricted to lines >= 469 -- two of which are the reversed pair, so nine survive under the rule 'one assertion = one assert/require call site'. Under an equally natural rule the number moves: excluding the two require.True(t, ok) decode-plumbing checks gives 9 and 7, and counting distinct claims rather than call sites gives fewer again. Separately the row is not discriminating: 'the nine still pass' is satisfied by any tree in which that file compiles green, so its named failing input ('keeping two and deleting seven') does NOT fail it -- deleting assertions makes a count wrong and the row asserts no count. Wrong if: §6a named the file and function and defined the counting rule, and test 18 asserted the count rather than the passing.
suggestion: In §6a item 1 write: 'The gate guard is TestAuditGate_NoEscapeHatchFromTheGate in internal/cli/audit_signal_test.go. Counting one assert./require. call site as one assertion, it holds eleven; the two at the top -- that tp set --workflow --project audit_converge_on=blocking exits non-zero, and that stdout+stderr contains "unknown workflow field: audit_converge_on" -- are reversed, and the other nine stand.' Then test 18 becomes: 'the gate guard still holds exactly eleven assert/require call sites, the two named ones now assert acceptance, and the file is green | deleting the seven that are inconvenient, which leaves a green file'.

finding: §6a requires three coordinated edits and never states the replacement text, and §7 test 19 inherits the gap: 'SKILL.md and REFERENCE.md both state a rule true under **both** values'. 'States a rule true under both values' is not a pass/fail predicate -- no assertion can evaluate the truth of an arbitrary English sentence under two configurations. Two engineers write contradictory tests from that row: one asserts the ABSENCE of the old sentence, one asserts a SPECIFIC new sentence they invented, and both claim the row implemented. The guard the row names asserts literals (§6a itself says so: 'once as a test-local literal against SKILL.md's own prose, and once as engine.DivergenceHint against REFERENCE.md'), so the release cannot be built without the literal, and the spec is the only place it can be decided once for three artifacts that §6a says must move together. Wrong if: §6a gave the replacement sentence.
suggestion: State the sentence in §6a and have test 19 assert it verbatim. E.g.: 'The replacement, used verbatim in all three places: "Audit convergence counts every non-PASS row whose severity blocks under the resolved audit_converge_on; under the default all, that is every non-PASS row."' Then test 19 reads: 'SKILL.md, REFERENCE.md and engine.DivergenceHint all carry §6a's replacement sentence verbatim, asserted twice and independently by the docs-contract guard | editing the constant alone, which leaves SKILL.md green and false'.

finding: §2 says 'Both audit sinks compute next_action from the round's clean' and that the new branch 'names how many non-PASS rows were accepted'. §7 test 10 asserts one recommendation, names no sink, and pins the count only as 'names how many'. Test 12 shows §7 knows how to close this ('three assertions, one per path'); test 10 does not, so an implementation that changes the branch on --record and leaves --status on the old text passes it. And 'names how many' is not a form: '3 findings accepted' and 'three findings accepted' both satisfy it, so two engineers write assertions that disagree on whether a decimal numeral is required -- and a substring check for the count is what the test must do, since the row's own falsifying input is a text difference. Wrong if: §2 said which sink carries the sentence, or test 10 said 'on both --record and --status' and named the form.
suggestion: Rewrite test 10: 'under blocking, a clean round holding k non-PASS rows produces a recommendation on **both** --record and --status containing the decimal numeral k, textually different from the one an empty round produces -- two assertions, one per sink | deriving the branch from clean alone, or changing one sink and leaving the other'. Add one sentence to §2's next_action paragraph: 'The count appears as a decimal numeral, so a test can assert it as a substring.'

finding: §7's fourth column is headed 'the input that makes it fail', and its twenty cells hold four different kinds of thing, three of which cannot be run. Actual inputs -- a value to feed the system: row 11 ('recording at 1'). Mutants -- a change to production code to apply and watch fail: rows 1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 9b, 10, 14, 15, 16, 17. Descriptions of an inadequate TEST rather than of wrong code: rows 3 ('one test covering one sink while the other path ships ungraded'), 12 ('fencing one file, which leaves the others open'), 18 ('keeping two and deleting seven'). A historical anecdote that cannot be applied at all: row 4 ('v0.31.0 shipped the twin without both and needed v0.31.1'). And row 7's cell is a bare em-dash with no legend, so it is unresolvable between 'no input can falsify this' -- in which case the row is a tautology and a predicate that reports every round unclean passes it -- and 'to be decided'. The column's whole value is that a reader can APPLY the cell and watch the row go red; §7's own framing paragraph says a decision that changes and leaves its row untouched becomes visible, which only holds if the cell is runnable. Wrong if: the header read 'what makes it fail' and a legend defined the em-dash.
suggestion: Rename the column 'the mutant that must fail it' and make every cell applicable. Replace row 4's cell with 'a resolver that emits the field from --extract but accepts any string in validate --project'. Replace row 7's em-dash with 'a predicate that reports every round unclean, which rows 5 and 6 catch only if they assert *clean* under blocking rather than not-clean under all'. Add a legend line under the table: 'Every cell names a change to production code or to a fixture that must make that row's assertion fail. A row whose cell cannot be applied is not yet a test.'

finding: §2.1 spends a paragraph establishing that the table's cells 'are reachable only when the field resolves before round 1 is recorded', because §2 stamps clean at record time and a round recorded before the knob is set 'keeps clean: false for ever'. §7 test 11 says 'replaying ... recorded rounds from committed testdata reproduces the table' and never states that precondition, so the replay's procedure is unpinned in exactly the dimension §2.1 says decides the numbers: an implementer who records round 1 under the default and then sets blocking gets different cells and cannot tell whether the code, the fixture or the procedure is wrong. The row is also unpinned on ordering: §7's closing paragraph lists the projected fields as status, severity, role and item_id, none of which carries a round ordinal, while the assertion is entirely about which round number the streak reaches. Wrong if: test 11 stated that the replay records every round with the field already resolved, and the projection paragraph preserved a round key.
suggestion: Extend test 11's assertion: 'replaying v0.35.0's nine and v0.36.0's thirteen recorded rounds from committed testdata -- **each round recorded with audit_converge_on already resolved, per §2.1** -- reproduces the table ... at audit_clean_rounds: 2'. And extend §7's projection paragraph: 'The projection keeps status, severity, role, item_id and the round's ordinal, one file per round, named audit-round-N.ndjson under a per-cycle directory in the test's own testdata tree.'

finding: Two normative clauses of this release have no row deriving from them, in a §7 whose opening sentence is 'Every test here is derived from a numbered decision above'. (a) §2: invalid values are refused 'on the same terms and with the same hint as review_converge_on'. Test 3 asserts the two error KINDS -- usage error at the write sink, validation error at the consuming sink -- and says nothing about the hint, so hint parity ships unasserted. That is the exact class of config/doc parity that cost this project v0.31.1, which test 4's own cell cites as the reason test 4 exists. (b) §2.1: 'skills/tp/SKILL.md carries the one-line command that derives it, next to the field's documentation.' That is a deliverable of this release, the spec never states the command, and no row derives from it -- while the docs-contract guard §6a already reaches SKILL.md, so it is the cheapest assertion in the release and is currently asserted nowhere. Wrong if: test 3 named the hint, and §2.1 stated the command.
suggestion: Extend test 3: '... a validation error -- and both messages carry the same hint text review_converge_on's sinks emit, with this field's name substituted | asserting the exit codes only'. State the command in §2.1 as a literal, then add row 4b: '| 4b | §2.1 *the number the operator needs* | skills/tp/SKILL.md carries §2.1's derivation command verbatim, beside the field's documentation, asserted by the docs-contract guard | documenting the field without the command, which leaves the operator no basis for the decision |'.

finding: §7 test 2's assertion reads 'task override beats project config beats built-in; no CLI or environment layer is asserted, because none exists'. 'is asserted' is ambiguous between 'the test asserts that no such layer exists' and 'the test makes no assertion about such a layer'. One engineer writes a case proving TP_AUDIT_CONVERGE_ON=blocking is ignored; the other writes nothing and calls the row done. The two readings differ in whether the release ships a regression guard on its own precedence, and this repository has already been wrong about this precedence once -- CLAUDE.md records the five-layer claim being removed from this spec at review round 4, and records a sibling spec whose audit spent two rounds unable to verify the top two layers. A row that leaves 'is asserted' undecided is how that error survives into the tests. Wrong if: the cell read 'and a test asserts that TP_AUDIT_CONVERGE_ON and an --audit-converge-on flag are both unrecognised', or 'and no layer beyond these three is tested'.
suggestion: Pick one reading and write it. Recommended, because it guards the error this spec has already made once: 'task override beats project config beats built-in -- three assertions -- and a fourth asserts that TP_AUDIT_CONVERGE_ON=blocking in the environment leaves the resolved value at the layer below it | a resolver reading only the project layer, or an environment layer added silently'.

finding: §2's clearest new observable -- 'Under blocking a round can record clean: true beside a non-zero open, and that is correct' -- sits on §7's 'Not tested here, named so the absence is deliberate' list, justified as 'severity-blind by §2's boundary; spec/0.46.0.md §8 owns changing that'. §8 owns CHANGING the streaks. It does not own asserting that THIS release preserves them while making clean diverge from open for the first time in tp's history, which is the release's whole behavioural signature. The exclusion therefore defers a regression assertion under cover of deferring a feature, and it is the cheapest assertion available: test 10 already builds the fixture that produces it. Wrong if: §7's exclusion paragraph said the clean/open pairing is asserted here and only the future severity-awareness deferred.
suggestion: Move the pairing off the exclusion list and into the table: '| 10b | §2 *boundary* | under blocking, one round reports clean: true and a non-zero role_streaks[].open on the same payload, and spec_coverage_clean_rounds counts that round | making the streaks severity-aware, which zeroes open and hides the divergence |'. Keep the exclusion paragraph for the future change only, rewording it to 'making the streaks severity-aware is deferred; that they stay severity-blind here is test 10b.'
